name: Framer Framed
funding: Ministry of OCW, Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst, Stadsdeel Oost and VriendenLoterij Fonds, per its about page.
watch: Decolonial art platform founded in 2009. The Rabo ArtLab project is in no source I opened.
records_note: Framer Framed names its six-member supervisory board and four public funders on undated pages, but posts no annual reports or accounts.

name: Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and Museum
watch: Founded 1971 at 37 Holden Road, North Finchley; the largest Belarusian collection in western Europe; governed by a board of trustees; dormant and deregistered 2011, revived 2014 and re-registered 27 Apr 2015.
records_note: Annual reports for 2020, 2024 and 2025 are on its site, accounts are with the Charity Commission, trustees are listed, and no donors are named.

name: Franco-Namibian Cultural Centre (FNCC)
funding: Binational centre under Namibian law, funded by the French government. Namibia gave the land and France paid for the building; foundation stone laid in 1998.
watch: Has a large multipurpose gallery and hosts exhibitions at 118 Robert Mugabe Avenue, Windhoek.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list; its Team page names the director and staff but no board.

name: G.A.S. Foundation (Guest Artists Space)
funding: Primarily funded by the Yinka Shonibare Foundation at its 2019 launch. Donors include Terra Foundation, Deutsche Bank, Afreximbank, Still Earth Holdings, British Council and Pro Helvetia.
watch: Founded 2019 by Yinka Shonibare, who started the London residency Guest Projects. Patron Still Earth Holdings owns drilling contractor Tirex, an oil-services supplier.
records_note: Posts two impact reports (2022 to mid-2025), a named donor list and its trustees; accounts are filed by its UK parent, the Yinka Shonibare Foundation.

name: Gallery 1957
funding: Commercial gallery founded in 2016 by British Lebanese construction owner Marwan Zakhem. Its Yaa Asantewaa Art Prize pays GHC 50,000 to the winner.
watch: Spaces in Accra and London. Zakhem's firm does oil and gas engineering and construction contracts and built the Kempinski hotel that houses the Accra gallery.
records_note: The private gallery's site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; the Yaa Asantewaa prize page credits one partner.

name: Gasworks
funding: £1.0M income (FY2026). Arts Council England £290k, City Bridge Foundation, Lambeth, British Council, Cockayne fund, Great Britain Sasakawa Foundation, Henry Moore Foundation, residency trusts and patrons.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Thank You page names funders undated, and nine trustees are listed.

name: Glenstone
watch: Mitchell Rales co-founded Danaher. A 2015 Senate inquiry examined 11 private museums, Glenstone among them, over founders' tax benefits.
records_note: No annual reports, donor list or board on its site; Form 990-PF filings for 2006 to 2024 are public on ProPublica.

name: Grazer Kunstverein
funding: Federal arts ministry, City of Graz and Land Steiermark culture department. Patrons: AVL List, Industriellenvereinigung Steiermark, Weitzer Hotels, legero united, Weingut Peter Skoff.
records_note: Names its patrons in text and its six board members, shows public funders as logos, and posts no annual report or accounts.

name: Gudskul (ruangrupa / Serrum / Grafis Huru Hara)
funding: Communal resource pool (lumbung), DOEN Foundation, Arts Collaboratory, and cooperative commercial enterprises. Completely non-corporate collective governance.
watch: Educational collective formed by ruangrupa (curators of documenta fifteen), Serrum and Grafis Huru Hara. It developed the 'lumbung' practice of shared resources, collective decision-making and communal art-making.
records_note: Its site publishes no annual report, accounts, board or funder names; the about page says only that donors, sponsors and its own units pay.

name: Hangar.org
funding: Generalitat de Catalunya Department of Culture, Ajuntament de Barcelona, European cultural research programs. Non-profit artist association.
watch: Artist-run center for visual arts research and production in Poblenou.

name: Heide Museum of Modern Art
funding: Creative Victoria, Creative Australia and Manningham Council. Tucker, Gordon Darling, Downer and Shine On foundations; North East Link Community Fund; Melbourne Water; law, design and media sponsors.
watch: Established at the former home of John and Sunday Reed in Bulleen, Victoria.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2003 and audited 2024 accounts, names donors in its 2024 report and lists its seven-member board.

name: HEK (Haus der Elektronischen Künste)
funding: Small foundation-run house (2025); carried by the Christoph Merian Stiftung, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft and the Federal Office of Culture.
watch: Building is at Freilager-Platz 9 in Münchenstein. Education is funded by Göhner and Binding; the Pax Art Awards by Art Foundation Pax, an insurer's foundation.
records_note: HEK posts annual reports for 2021 to 2025 and names its foundation board, but shows funders as logos and publishes no accounts.
